raw.excerpt: European roles, your afternoon hours.  No night shift.
raw.description:
European roles, your afternoon hours. No night shift. If you recruit for foreign clients from the Philippines, this is the same game, paid per placement in euros. Open to recruiters based in Davao City and across the Philippines.

Read all of this before you apply. It's long on purpose. If this isn't you, that's completely fine, and it saves us both time.

Who we are

BC Recruitment places people in jobs across Europe: multilingual customer service, sales and support roles with some of the biggest international employers, in cities like Athens, Lisbon, Porto, Braga and Sofia. Many of these jobs come with relocation help, which makes them easier to sell to candidates.

We have around 60 open roles right now, in Dutch, German, French, Italian, Spanish, Polish, Turkish, the Nordic languages and more. Alongside those we have specialist roles, like compliance, legal and tech, that pay a lot more per placement.

You don't need to speak the candidates' languages. Every role needs English, and English is what we work in. What matters is that you know where to find people and how to get them excited about a job abroad.

Who we're looking for

People who are hungry, driven and excited about this opportunity, and who believe they can earn more on commission than they do now.

We don't care how many years you've been recruiting. Someone with 6 months of hunger can beat someone with 10 years of experience. We care about what you have personally delivered: how many placements, for what kind of roles, and how many a month.

You'll probably fit if:

  • You understand that every nationality is found differently. If one channel doesn't work for a market, you know where those people really are and go there.
  • You already have your own tools: LinkedIn, laptop, phone, and whatever else you use to recruit.
  • You want freedom: your own hours, your own place, your own methods, no boss.
  • You have real numbers: placements or sales you made yourself, and you know your monthly average.
  • You've done global or international recruitment, ideally for similar companies or the same kind of candidates: customer service, call centres, multilingual roles, relocation, tourism, hospitality.
  • You're a natural seller who finds people on your own, without leads or hand-holding.

This is NOT for you if

  • You need us to pay for tools before you can work. We don't cover anything at the start.
  • You want something to try "when you have time".
  • You need someone to tell you what to do every day.
  • You'll blame others when a client pauses a role or a candidate drops out. That's part of recruitment.
  • Most of the people you can reach need a visa. Most of our roles require candidates who can already work in the EU, and we don't offer visa support on most jobs.
  • You need a fixed income soon. There is no salary, retainer or paid trial at the start.

What you earn

  • Minimum €400 per placement. Most roles pay €400–750, and specialist roles up to €2,400.
  • You see the exact payout on every role before you work on it.
  • A placement counts once your candidate has started and the employer has paid us. Someone who accepts and then drops out is not a placement.
  • Payment usually comes 1–3 months after your candidate starts, depending on the employer. We pay by bank transfer or whatever works for you.
  • Money you've earned is always paid. We know many recruiters are afraid of not being paid. Think about it from our side: a recruiter who delivers is worth far more to us over time than any single placement. This whole system is built on trust, and we'd lose by breaking it.

If you deliver, we deliver back

Nothing is given up front. Everything grows with your results, for proven partners and agreed case by case:

  • Once you deliver, we cover tool costs such as monthly subscriptions.
  • Proven recruiters can get earlier payouts, arranged with you.
  • Consistent performers can earn a monthly base on top of commission.

The rules bend toward the people who prove themselves. This job gets better the more you deliver.

What you get from day one

  • Proper onboarding: we explain everything, the employers, the roles and how we work, and answer all your questions before you start, so you begin with confidence.
  • Full role details and answers to the questions candidates usually ask.
  • Direct contact with us whenever you have a question about a role or a candidate.
  • Total freedom over how, when and where you work.

What's realistic

  • The first weeks are about building your pipeline.
  • Once you're up and running, a below-average recruiter makes about 1 placement a month, a good recruiter 2–5, and our best recruiters 5–10. It gets easier over time: you build a pool of candidates to come back to, and people start recommending you.
  • We expect at least one placement a month once you're up and running.

How we choose

  1. You answer the questions below. We read every answer.
  2. If your answers are strong, we have a video call.
  3. If we're a fit, we onboard you.

Everyone starts with a 30-day trial. Show real progress in that month, with candidates submitted and in interviews, and you stay and grow. If not, we part ways with no hard feelings.

To apply, answer these questions

  1. Your numbers. How many placements have you made per month on average, and for which roles and countries? What was your best month?
  2. The task. We have a Dutch-speaking customer service role in Athens, and candidates must already be allowed to work in the EU. Where exactly would you find 5 of them within two weeks, and how? Name the real channels, groups or searches you'd use.
  3. Commission. Why do you prefer being paid per placement over a salary, or over how you've been paid before?
  4. Your setup. Which tools and channels do you use today? How many hours a week can you put in, and what else are you working on right now?

Apply here with your CV. Then email your answers to , with your name and country in the subject. Applications without answers aren't reviewed.

Optional: attach a voice note or video answering "Why should we pick you?" It's the quickest way for us to get to know you.

Be specific: numbers, names, real examples. Answers that sound AI-written, or that just say what you think we want to hear, are rejected.

raw.description:
NVIDIA's invention of the GPU in 1999 sparked the growth of the PC gaming market, redefined modern computer graphics, and revolutionized parallel computing. GPU deep learning ignited the modern AI era, with NVIDIA hardware and software acting as the foundation for the world's most ambitious AI, robotics, and autonomous systems workloads. Today, we are the AI computing company. NVIDIA Data Center Systems, including DGX, HGX, and MGX platforms, deliver the world's leading infrastructure for AI at scale. We are growing our teams with the most thoughtful, creative, and driven people on the planet.


NVIDIA is searching for a highly motivated and creative senior security firmware engineer to join the Data Center Systems Software team and secure the platform: the baseboard management controllers, microcontrollers, and silicon roots of trust the rest of the platform depends on. You will design and deliver the firmware that proves the integrity of NVIDIA's data center systems from the first instruction out of reset through attestation, update, and recovery in production, and set technical direction for work that spans silicon vendors, platform teams, and industry standards bodies.


What you'll be doing:

  • Derive security requirements for NVIDIA’s data center platforms from business needs and threat modeling.
  • Design and deliver root of trust firmware with features like secure and measured boot, attestation, provisioning of identities and cryptographic material, and secure debug.
  • Own features from architecture to code: make the trade-offs explicit, gain agreement across silicon, platform, security architecture, manufacturing, and partner teams, and deliver the implementation.
  • Implement industry security standards (eg.: SPDM, TCG DICE).
  • Lead design and code reviews, improve threat modeling, testing, CI, and release practices, and make AI agents a normal part of how the team builds firmware.

What we need to see:

  • BS or MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 7+ years of software and firmware engineering experience, or equivalent depth, including products built on a hardware root of trust.
  • Deep understanding of roof of trust security fundamentals: chains of trust, signing and key management, attestation, and anti-rollback.
  • Strong low-level programming skills and a deep understanding of SoC access controls (privilege levels, TrustZone, memory and bus protection).
  • Familiarity with server firmware and systems software, plus experience building automation using Python or a comparable language.
  • A record of leading technical work across teams without formal authority, including guiding other engineers on a shared deliverable.
  • Experience with modern AI and agents, including an AI-forward mindset and proactive adoption of new tools and techniques.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a strong preference for written communication that creates clarity and institutional memory for a distributed team.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and complexity; you make sound decisions quickly with incomplete information and course-correct without friction.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Contributions to open-source root of trust projects or to industry security standards.
  • Experience building systems with symmetric, asymmetric, and post-quantum cryptography.
  • Rust firmware experience, including bringing Rust into an existing C or C++ codebase.
  • Secure Manufacturing at scale. Security certifications such as FIPS 140-3.
  • Hardware cryptographic accelerators, secure key storage, trusted execution frameworks such as OP-TEE or Keystone, and OpenBMC.

NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world's most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people on the planet working for us. If you're creative and autonomous, we want to hear from you!

Multilingual recruiting for Europe, from home, paid in euros per placement. Open to recruiters based in Cairo and across Egypt.

Read all of this before you apply. It's long on purpose. If this isn't you, that's completely fine, and it saves us both time.

Who we are

BC Recruitment places people in jobs across Europe: multilingual customer service, sales and support roles with some of the biggest international employers, in cities like Athens, Lisbon, Porto, Braga and Sofia. Many of these jobs come with relocation help, which makes them easier to sell to candidates.

We have around 60 open roles right now, in Dutch, German, French, Italian, Spanish, Polish, Turkish, the Nordic languages and more. Alongside those we have specialist roles, like compliance, legal and tech, that pay a lot more per placement.

You don't need to speak the candidates' languages. Every role needs English, and English is what we work in. What matters is that you know where to find people and how to get them excited about a job abroad.

Who we're looking for

People who are hungry, driven and excited about this opportunity, and who believe they can earn more on commission than they do now.

We don't care how many years you've been recruiting. Someone with 6 months of hunger can beat someone with 10 years of experience. We care about what you have personally delivered: how many placements, for what kind of roles, and how many a month.

You'll probably fit if:

  • You've done global or international recruitment, ideally for similar companies or the same kind of candidates: customer service, call centres, multilingual roles, relocation, tourism, hospitality.
  • You're a natural seller who finds people on your own, without leads or hand-holding.
  • You understand that every nationality is found differently. If one channel doesn't work for a market, you know where those people really are and go there.
  • You already have your own tools: LinkedIn, laptop, phone, and whatever else you use to recruit.
  • You want freedom: your own hours, your own place, your own methods, no boss.
  • You have real numbers: placements or sales you made yourself, and you know your monthly average.

This is NOT for you if

  • You want something to try "when you have time".
  • You need someone to tell you what to do every day.
  • You'll blame others when a client pauses a role or a candidate drops out. That's part of recruitment.
  • Most of the people you can reach need a visa. Most of our roles require candidates who can already work in the EU, and we don't offer visa support on most jobs.
  • You need a fixed income soon. There is no salary, retainer or paid trial at the start.
  • You need us to pay for tools before you can work. We don't cover anything at the start.

What you earn

  • Minimum €400 per placement. Most roles pay €400–750, and specialist roles up to €2,400.
  • You see the exact payout on every role before you work on it.
  • A placement counts once your candidate has started and the employer has paid us. Someone who accepts and then drops out is not a placement.
  • Payment usually comes 1–3 months after your candidate starts, depending on the employer. We pay by bank transfer or whatever works for you.
  • Money you've earned is always paid. We know many recruiters are afraid of not being paid. Think about it from our side: a recruiter who delivers is worth far more to us over time than any single placement. This whole system is built on trust, and we'd lose by breaking it.

If you deliver, we deliver back

Nothing is given up front. Everything grows with your results, for proven partners and agreed case by case:

  • Once you deliver, we cover tool costs such as monthly subscriptions.
  • Proven recruiters can get earlier payouts, arranged with you.
  • Consistent performers can earn a monthly base on top of commission.

The rules bend toward the people who prove themselves. This job gets better the more you deliver.

What you get from day one

  • Proper onboarding: we explain everything, the employers, the roles and how we work, and answer all your questions before you start, so you begin with confidence.
  • Full role details and answers to the questions candidates usually ask.
  • Direct contact with us whenever you have a question about a role or a candidate.
  • Total freedom over how, when and where you work.

What's realistic

  • The first weeks are about building your pipeline.
  • Once you're up and running, a below-average recruiter makes about 1 placement a month, a good recruiter 2–5, and our best recruiters 5–10. It gets easier over time: you build a pool of candidates to come back to, and people start recommending you.
  • We expect at least one placement a month once you're up and running.

How we choose

  1. You answer the questions below. We read every answer.
  2. If your answers are strong, we have a video call.
  3. If we're a fit, we onboard you.

Everyone starts with a 30-day trial. Show real progress in that month, with candidates submitted and in interviews, and you stay and grow. If not, we part ways with no hard feelings.

To apply, answer these questions

  1. Your numbers. How many placements have you made per month on average, and for which roles and countries? What was your best month?
  2. The task. We have a Dutch-speaking customer service role in Athens, and candidates must already be allowed to work in the EU. Where exactly would you find 5 of them within two weeks, and how? Name the real channels, groups or searches you'd use.
  3. Commission. Why do you prefer being paid per placement over a salary, or over how you've been paid before?
  4. Your setup. Which tools and channels do you use today? How many hours a week can you put in, and what else are you working on right now?

Apply here with your CV. Then email your answers to , with your name and country in the subject. Applications without answers aren't reviewed.

Optional: attach a voice note or video answering "Why should we pick you?" It's the quickest way for us to get to know you.

Be specific: numbers, names, real examples. Answers that sound AI-written, or that just say what you think we want to hear, are rejected.

About Schneider Geospatial

Schneider Geospatial is a GovTech software company helping local governments serve their communities through solutions spanning parcel management, permitting and licensing, and asset management. Our team partners with public agencies to improve transparency, efficiency, and service delivery.

The Opportunity

The Geographic Account Executive owns commercial growth across an assigned territory, including winning new local-government customers, expanding relationships and solutions within existing accounts, and proactively identifying commercial retention risks. This is a market-owner role: you will build a territory strategy, create demand, lead complex sales cycles, and mobilize Schneider colleagues to deliver customer value. Success is measured by sustainable ARR growth, not simply activity or inherited pipeline.

This role offers the autonomy to operate as the commercial leader of an established geographic market, combining a meaningful installed customer base with substantial opportunity for new customer acquisition. You'll have the ability to shape your territory strategy, develop lasting customer relationships, and directly influence Schneider Geospatial's growth.

What You Will Do

    Own the market and build a growth plan

  • Develop and execute an annual territory strategy grounded in local-government market dynamics, installed-base penetration, whitespace, competitive footprint, and priority segments.
  • Prioritize geographic markets, agencies, buyer personas, and solution plays; maintain an actionable account and prospect plan.

    • Create and win new business

  • Generate qualified opportunities through proactive outreach, referrals, conferences, partner relationships, marketing programs, and compelling customer use cases.
  • Lead discovery, quantify business problems, identify replacement triggers, build consensus across stakeholders, and manage the full opportunity through negotiation and close.
  • Position Schneider solutions against incumbent processes and competing platforms, partnering with product and solution specialists as appropriate.

    • Grow and protect the installed base

  • Build relationships with current customers across departments and leadership levels to identify cross-sell, expansion, and reference opportunities.
  • Stay aware of customer health, renewal and competitive risks; coordinate with Support, Professional Services, and other owners to address issues while retaining commercial accountability.
  • Lead commercial discussions for assigned accounts, including expansion, contract transitions, and renewal-related opportunities in accordance with company policy.

    • Execute with discipline and collaboration

  • Maintain accurate account, activity, opportunity, next-step, and forecast information in Salesforce and sales engagement tools.
  • Manage pipeline creation, qualified coverage, opportunity progression, and ARR bookings against established performance expectations.
  • Collaborate with Marketing, Sales Operations, product specialists, Support, and Professional Services; coordinate proposals, pricing, approvals, and contracting.

What We Are Looking For

  • Demonstrated success in consultative B2B or B2G software sales, including prospecting, competitive selling, negotiation, and closing.
  • Ability to manage both net-new acquisition and strategic expansion of existing customers without losing focus on pipeline creation.
  • Strong territory planning, account prioritization, business acumen, and disciplined CRM/forecast management.
  • Ability to navigate complex, multi-stakeholder sales processes; experience selling to county or municipal government is strongly preferred.
  • Knowledge of local-government workflows, GIS, parcel management, permitting, or asset management is a plus.
  • Excellent discovery, presentation, relationship-building, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
  • Comfort with regular travel (typically 25%-30%) throughout the assigned territory and attendance at industry events.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience; 3–5+ years of relevant sales experience preferred.

How Success Will Be Evaluated

    ARR bookings and territory growth; qualified pipeline creation and coverage; new-logo acquisition; existing-customer expansion; opportunity progression and forecast quality; and proactive management of commercial retention risks. Specific quotas, metrics, and account assignments are established separately.

Role Boundaries

    The Geographic Account Executive owns the commercial strategy and customer relationship within the assigned geography, working alongside specialist sales roles when appropriate. Technical support, implementation delivery, and day-to-day service case resolution remain with their respective functional teams.

Equal Opportunity

Schneider Geospatial is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and believe that diversity strengthens our team, fuels innovation, and drives success.

raw.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz, All About Cookies, and OnlyInYourState. We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies.

Our mission: create predictable, high-value customer acquisition at scale by connecting discovery, intent, and performance across category-leading consumer brands in finance, travel, and entertainment.

We run profitable and bootstrapped, with a South Florida HQ and a remote-first team across 18 countries.

WHY JOIN US?

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. The pace is real, and change is constant, so the people who do best turn change into opportunity instead of waiting for it to settle. Feedback runs direct and lands with respect. Ordinary people make themselves extraordinary at Launch Potato.

THE ROLE

We're looking for a hands-on Partnerships & BD expert to grow our banking, deposits, and investing partners, and to bring on the ones we haven't met yet. Most of the job, roughly 70 to 80 percent, is growing the partners we already have: bigger budgets, better economics, broader distribution. The rest is net new, mostly warm, with real outreach on the investing side where the relationships don't exist yet.

You'll work alongside our Head of Partnerships, who will continue to focus on our largest strategic partners. On those strategic partners, you'll run the operations. Across the rest of banking, deposits, and investing, you own it fully, operationally and strategically. That's what gives the Head of Partnerships room for the biggest bets, and it's what makes this seat yours.

This isn't a support role, and it isn't customer service. The job is to grow relationships, not just service them.

WHY THIS SEAT

  • A category to own. Banking, deposits, and investing partners outside our largest strategic accounts are yours, start to finish.
  • A partner, not a handoff. Our Head of Partnerships works closely alongside you for your first 90 days, and the goal is full independence by about day 120.
  • Room to shape it. You'll inherit real momentum, but the strategy in these categories is still being written, and you'll help write it.
  • Close to the media. You'll connect what partners need to placements across FinanceBuzz and our publisher network, which is where a good partnership becomes an extraordinary one.
  • Direct exposure to senior leadership on the deals that matter.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

  • Direct experience on the advertiser side of a financial comparison publisher, marketplace, or performance network, managing bank, deposit, or investing partners.
  • A record of growing accounts, not just servicing them. You can walk through a partner whose budget you grew and what moved it.
  • Sales DNA. You open doors and close. Warm relationships are most of it, but you're comfortable with cold outreach, especially to investing apps.
  • Ownership of the details. URL approvals, budget changes, CPA moves, placement and widget coordination: you run them yourself and nothing drops.
  • You figure it out without being pushed, and you pull in account management, product, media, analytics, compliance, legal, and finance to get it done.
  • Fluency in performance economics, including CPA, CPL, CPC, and revenue share, and the business acumen to use performance, revenue, and unit-economic data in a negotiation.
  • Strong communication, relationship building, and negotiation across several partners and opportunities at once.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Publisher experience, or enough of the language to hold the conversation.
  • Experience in wealth management, financial advisory, RIAs, or advisor networks.
  • Existing relationships with banks, fintech companies, investment platforms, or related financial-services companies.
  • Experience selling customer acquisition, media, lead generation, or performance-based marketing.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

Existing partners

  • Budget growth, better unit economics, broader product coverage, and a bigger share of wallet with the partners you own.
  • The operations on our largest strategic banking partners, alongside the Head of Partnerships.
  • Partner operations from onboarding through campaign management, reporting, issue resolution, and optimization.
  • Proposals that connect a partner's goals to placements, audiences, and distribution across FinanceBuzz and our publisher network.
  • Accurate pipeline, forecasts, partner updates, and next steps.
  • Launch Potato's presence at industry events and partner meetings.

New partners

  • A pipeline across banking, deposits, investing, and wealth.
  • Reaching the right decision makers through relationships, referrals, events, and outbound.
  • Partner conversations from first outreach through pitch, deal negotiation, contracting, and launch.
  • A clear read on each partner's growth goals, economics, products, and target customers.

WHAT GREAT LOOKS LIKE

  • First 90 days: you're learning the book side by side with the Head of Partnerships and running operations on the partners you'll own.
  • By about day 120: you run your partners independently.
  • By month 6: you're directing internal traffic and connecting partner activity to media opportunity.
  • Year one: larger budgets and stronger economics across existing partners, new banks and investing advertisers live, and the Head of Partnerships focused on our largest, most strategic deals.

THIS ISN'T THE RIGHT SEAT IF YOU

  • Want to hunt, close, and hand the account to someone else.
  • Want someone else to own the operations.
  • Need a playbook handed to you before you move.
  • Would rather service an account than grow it.

TOTAL COMPENSATION

  • Base: $150,000 to $170,000, set by level and expertise based on initial interviews.
  • Annual Bonus: company EBITDA plus personal performance. No commission.

Want to accelerate your career? Apply now!

Since day one, we've been committed to having a diverse, inclusive team and culture. We are proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity company. We value diversity, equity, and inclusion.

We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

raw.title: Accounts Receivable Specialist
raw.excerpt: The World We EnvisionI believe the work that gets care paid for matters as much as the work that gets a device to a patient's door.
raw.description:
The World We Envision

I believe the work that gets care paid for matters as much as the work that gets a device to a patient's door. When cash moves fast and clean, we say yes to the next patient sooner. I want every card run the day it's ready, every work comp invoice paid, and a weekly scoreboard that shows exactly who made it happen. If you've hit your numbers somewhere that only noticed when you missed them, you'll find that's not how it works here.

The Mission and Team

Right Coast Medical started in 2010 with one question from our founder, Brent Long: "What if pain relief didn't have to come with a risk of addiction?" Back then, opioids were the default after surgery. Brent thought families deserved better, and he built a company around non-opioid recovery devices like ThermX, T-REX and SAM 2.0.

Zach Holmes joined in 2014, fresh out of college. He helped grow RCM from a regional operation into a national provider, and today he runs it as our CEO. That's what this place does for people who take ownership.

You'll work with me, our CFO, and a small billing team that takes care of veterans and injured workers across the country. They get the claims right. You make sure the money comes in.

The Role: Accounts Receivable Specialist

You turn every VA card and work comp invoice into cash, fast and right, so we can keep our promise to providers and patients, and veterans and injured workers can recover without opioids and get back to what they love.

This is a new seat. Today our billers carry the back end of billing on top of the front end, and both jobs deserve a full-time owner. Getting paid isn't a project that ends. We built this role because we need it.

You'll love:

  • Running 500–750 VA card payments a month, each one charged, receipted and posted within one business day at 98%+ accuracy
  • Raising our work comp collection rate by 15 points in your first year
  • Cutting the time it takes a work comp invoice to turn into cash by 30% in your first six months
  • Bringing old balances back to life, so every aged invoice has a status, a contact and a next step
  • Freeing our billers to focus on getting claims right the first time
  • Seeing exactly where you stand on a weekly scoreboard, with no guessing about whether you're winning

Where this leads

As RCM grows, this seat can grow into a lead role, or
move up into billing. I won't promise you a title. I will promise that your results will be seen, and that the people who get promoted here are the ones who own their numbers.

Along the way, you'll learn work comp billing end to end, from the invoice to the adjuster to the cash. You'll become the person who knows where every dollar stands and what it will take to bring it in.

About You

  • You have 2+ years of work comp, medical, or third-party collections experience. Adjusters and TPAs don't rattle you.
  • Before anything goes out, you check every amount, card and receipt.
  • Today's queue gets cleared today.
  • You follow up until it's paid: politely, on schedule, every time.
  • No open item on your desk lacks a next step and a date.
  • When an adjuster pushes back, you hold the line without caving or getting heated.
  • Patient and card data stay protected because that's your habit, not because someone is watching.
  • Excel and QuickBooks Online feel familiar. Salesforce, Breadwinner and PayTrace
    you'll learn with us.

This is not for you if:

  • You need someone checking in to stay on task. This is remote, and the scoreboard does the talking.
  • "Close enough" is close enough.
  • You'd rather send one email and wait than pick up the phone.

Pay and Terms

  • $25.00/hour to start, hourly and overtime-eligible
  • $26.44/hour at day 90, once you hit your first 90-day goals
  • Quarterly bonus of up to $1,500 ($6,000/year), tied to work comp collection results
  • Full-time, remote (U.S.), Monday–Friday, roughly 8–5 in your time zone, with some flexibility as long as you're working mostly during business hours
  • 15 days paid PTO, 5 sick days, and paid holidays
  • 401(k)

If you're reading this and saying "HECK YEAH," we want to meet you.

Salary: $25/hr

Overview The Senior Vice President of Finance serves as the strategic financial leader for the Infrastructure business, driving financial performance, governance, and long-term growth across a diverse portfolio of operations. Reporting to the CE&I CFO, with a matrix relationship to the Infrastructure EVP, this role leads the finance organization through a team of VP-level leaders and provides executive oversight of financial planning, forecasting, budgeting, accounting operations, reporting, and compliance. As a trusted business partner to senior leadership, the SVP plays a critical role in shaping strategy, optimizing performance, and supporting disciplined growth. Our Infrastructure business includes heavy civil construction and public infrastructure projects such as roadway and bridge construction, paving and asphalt operations, heavy civil site development, underground utility installation, environmental remediation, earthwork and grading, transportation infrastructure, DOT-funded projects, and the production of ready-mix concrete and aggregate materials. Location: This role offers location flexibility and may be based anywhere within the Continental United States. Travel: Up to 50% travel is required to provide on-site leadership, strengthen business partnerships, and support operations across a geographically diverse Infrastructure organization. Company Overview MasTec’s Clean Energy & Infrastructure (CE&I) segment generates more than $4.5 billion in annual revenue, providing construction services across our operating groups: Renewables, Industrial, Infrastructure and General Building. Our Renewables expertise includes solar, wind, energy storage, aftermarket services, substations and switchyards. Our Industrial expertise includes manufacturing, mining and mineral processing, power plants, conventional power generation, alternative fuel generation and other innovative solutions. In Infrastructure, we specialize in electrical, environmental, highways, roads and bridges, aggregate mining, ports and terminals, rail, pump and lift stations, water transmission and pipelines, water and wastewater treatment plants, and stormwater. Our General Building expertise includes airports, seaport terminals, sports and entertainment, pre-engineered metal buildings, and data centers. MasTec is a minority‑owned Fortune 500 construction company with more than 90 years of industry experience. With over 35,000 employees and 400 offices nationwide, we deliver complex infrastructure projects across the country. Safety and sustainability are core to how we operate. MasTec is proudly ranked by Engineering News‑Record as #1 in Power, #16 Top 50 Domestic Heavy Contractors, and #13 Transportation Contractor. The Clean Energy & Infrastructure Group comprises the following market sectors and operating companies: Renewables: IEA Constructors, Wanzek Construction, White Construction; Industrial: Phoenix Industrial, MasTec Industrial; Infrastructure: American Civil Constructors West Coast, Cash Construction, FNF Construction, MasTec Civil, Precision Aggregate Products, Ragnar Benson Construction, Saiia Construction, William Charles Construction, William Charles Electric; General Building: Lemartec, NV2A; and McKee Utility Contractors. Responsibilities Strategic & Executive Leadership Serve as a core member of the CE&I finance leadership team. Participate in I&I Group strategy development and execution. Provide financial insights to drive disciplined capital allocation and business performance. Partner closely with operational leaders to improve financial transparency and accountability. Financial Management & Reporting Lead annual budgeting, long-range planning, forecasting, and operating reviews. Oversee timely and accurate internal and external financial reporting. Ensure proper implementation of accounting policies and evolving internal controls. Maintain compliance with SOX and technical accounting standards. Oversee revenue recognition processes, particularly percentage-of-completion accounting for construction contracts. Project Controls & Risk Management Drive rigorous project financial management and risk mitigation processes. Enhance visibility into job-level profitability, cost controls, and margin performance. Support bid reviews and pricing decisions to improve win quality and risk-adjusted returns. Finance Operations & Transformation Lead finance operations across Infrastrtucture, focusing on process redesign and continuous improvement. Evaluate and deploy ERP systems and business enablement software solutions. Implement scalable systems and controls suitable for a rapidly expanding platform. Oversee integration of finance teams, systems, and processes following acquisitions. Talent & Organizational Development Develop strategic talent planning initiatives in partnership with HR. Mentor and coach high-performing finance leaders across business units. Build strong succession plans across all key finance roles. Foster a culture of integrity, transparency, accountability, and continuous improvement. In the first 12 months, the successful candidate will: Establish credibility with Infrastructure operational leaders and CE&I executive leadership. Develop a comprehensive understanding of project economics, systems, and reporting structures. Identify and prioritize critical finance transformation and integration initiatives. Improve forecasting reliability and project margin visibility. Strengthen internal controls and reporting consistency across legacy platforms. Provide leadership specific to change management on processes and ERP consolidation. Elevate talent capabilities and build a cohesive finance organization across acquired entities. Qualifications Work Experience and Education 10+ years of senior financial management experience in a large, geographically dispersed Infrastructure EPC or industrial organization. Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, or Business CPA or CA designation preferred Experience within a large, publicly traded organization strongly preferred. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Take reasonable care of your own and others’ health and safety and of those who may be affected by the day-to-day delivery of this role by taking personal responsibility for working toward the Company’s Zero Injury principles Demonstrated success leading high-performing finance teams in complex, publicly traded and growth-oriented environments. Experience overseeing Joint Venture operations, project-based accounting, and percentage-of-completion revenue recognition. Proven track record leading finance transformation initiatives, ERP implementations, and post-acquisition finance integrations. Comprehensive knowledge of financial planning and analysis, budgeting, forecasting, accounting operations, financial reporting, internal controls, and regulatory compliance. Strong business acumen with the ability to translate financial insights into strategic and operational decision-making. Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills with a demonstrated ability to drive continuous improvement and operational excellence. Effective executive presence with outstanding communication, presentation, negotiation, and relationship management skills across all levels of the organization. Ability to analyze complex business, financial, operational, and regulatory issues, develop practical solutions, and deliver results in a dynamic environment. Experience leading cross-functional initiatives and managing multiple priorities while maintaining disciplined project execution. raw.description:
The Company
At Spartan Investment Group our mission is to improve lives through our values. We do this by finding value-add and opportunistic investments offering solid returns to our investors. Providing an opportunity to grow for our partners and creating lasting wealth for everyone with whom we conduct business is how we make our greatest contribution.
We specifically focus on self-storage projects capitalizing on amazing deals in other asset classes. In 2021, we were listed as the 5th fastest growing real estate company in the US and joined the list of the top 100 owners of self-storage. We are members of the Inc. 5000 fastest-growing private companies in America and in 2023 we were #13 in Denver Business Journals list of top places to work.
Mission
The mission of the Inside Sales Representative is to convert interested storage customers into completed rentals through timely, proactive follow-up and effective sales conversations. This role is responsible for engaging prospective customers who have previously expressed interest in storage, understanding their needs, overcoming objections, and guiding them through the rental process. Success means maximizing lead conversion, delivering an excellent customer experience, and driving revenue growth across the FreeUp Storage portfolio.
This role is open to candidates in the United States, excluding those residing in Alaska, California, Colorado, Maine, New York, and Washington.
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
  • Lead Conversion Rate: Measures the percentage of assigned leads successfully converted into completed rentals, with a team target of 75%.
  • Lead Response & Follow-Up: Measures the speed and consistency of outreach to assigned leads, ensuring timely engagement and maximizing conversion opportunities.
  • Rental Attachments: Measures the percentage of completed rentals enrolled in AutoPay and Protection Plans, targeting 90% adoption for each.
  • Customer Reviews: Measures the percentage of completed rentals resulting in Google reviews, targeting 60%.
  • Rental Accuracy & CRM Compliance: Measures the accuracy of rental documentation, customer records, and lead tracking, maintaining at least 99% accuracy.
Outcomes
  • Lead Conversion: Convert assigned leads into completed rentals, consistently working toward a 75% conversion target through proactive outreach and effective sales techniques.
  • Rapid Lead Response: Contact newly assigned leads within 3 minutes during scheduled working hours, ensuring timely engagement and maximizing rental opportunities.
  • Consistent Follow-Up: Execute structured follow-up through phone calls, text messages, and emails, maintaining engagement with prospective customers until they rent or are appropriately dispositioned.
  • Objection Handling: Identify and address customer concerns related to pricing, unit availability, sizing, and move-in timing, providing solutions that increase conversion and establish clear next steps.
  • AutoPay & Protection Plan Enrollment: Promote and secure AutoPay enrollment and Protection Plan participation on at least 90% of completed rentals.
  • Customer Reviews: Encourage satisfied customers to leave Google reviews, working toward a 60% review generation target while delivering a positive customer experience.
  • Rental Documentation & CRM Management: Complete rental documentation with at least 99% accuracy while maintaining detailed, up-to-date records of customer interactions, follow-up commitments, and lead dispositions.
  • Sales Performance: Consistently meet individual and team sales goals, leveraging weekly performance scorecards, coaching, and customer feedback to improve conversion rates and maximize rental volume.
Competencies
  • Salesmanship: Confidently guides customer conversations, overcomes objections, and effectively closes sales while maintaining a customer-focused approach.
  • Communication: Communicates clearly, professionally, and persuasively through phone, text, and email, adapting messaging to individual customer needs.
  • Persistence: Demonstrates resilience and determination in pursuing sales opportunities, maintaining consistent follow-up and a results-driven approach.
  • Customer Focus: Builds trust, understands customer needs, and recommends appropriate storage solutions that create a positive rental experience.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership of assigned leads, performance metrics, and follow-up commitments while consistently delivering on expectations.
  • Organization: Effectively manages multiple leads, prioritizes outreach activities, and maintains accurate records while meeting established response and performance expectations.
Qualifications
  • Minimum of 3 years of call center sales experience or 2 years of self-storage industry experience with a strong emphasis on sales and customer conversion.
  • Demonstrated history of meeting or exceeding sales quotas, with the ability to provide measurable results related to conversion rates, closed sales, or quota attainment.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to confidently engage customers over the phone and communicate professionally through text and email.
  • Proven ability to overcome objections, negotiate effectively, and close sales in a high-volume, customer-facing environment.
  • Proficiency with CRM systems, property management software, and general computer applications; experience with storEDGE is preferred.
  • High school diploma or GED required; additional college education preferred.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment with a quiet, private workspace, reliable high-speed internet, and availability for assigned shifts between 8:00 AM and 9:00 PM ET, Monday through Saturday.
Compensation & Benefit
  • Competitive Base Salary: $36,000–$43,000 annually, full-time, exempt.
  • Uncapped Bonus Potential: Opportunity to earn over 100% of base salary in additional compensation.
  • Promote Share Program: Opportunity to participate in the long-term success and growth of Spartan's investment portfolio.
  • Comprehensive Benefits: Company-paid health, dental, vision, short-term disability, and life insurance, with company contributions toward dependent and family coverage.
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan: Company matching contributions.
  • Cafeteria Plan: Annual reimbursement allowance for a variety of approved expenses, including entertainment, wellness, vehicle maintenance, and more.
  • Continuing Education: Reimbursement allowance to support continued professional development and skill-building related to your role.
  • Paid Time Off: PTO that increases with tenure and 8 paid holidays.
  • Performance & Wellness Incentives: Incentive programs that reward performance and personal well-being, supported by a dedicated performance and wellness coach to help employees achieve their personal and professional goals.

raw.description:
Provectus is an AI consultancy founded in 2010 and led by its founders. As an AWS Premier Partner and an Anthropic Preferred Partner, we help Financial Services & Insurance and Healthcare & Life Sciences companies design, build, and operate production AI systems. With offices across North America, LATAM, and EMEA, we work with clients worldwide.

We are hiring an Account Executive to turn incoming enterprise leads into signed consulting engagements. Clients buy multi-month consulting engagements. You won't build pipeline from scratch. Anthropic and AWS share qualified enterprise leads with us.

Your job has four parts:

  • Qualify those leads quickly.

  • Run discovery with buyers at banks, insurers and life sciences companies.

  • Scope the work with our architects.

  • Close.

What you'll do:

  • Pick up new leads as they arrive, decide which to pursue, and be able to explain why.

  • Run discovery calls with business and technology leaders. Map their process, data, regulatory constraints, budget and decision path.

  • Work with delivery leads and architects to scope proposals and SOWs that we can deliver. You are selling consulting engagements, not software licenses.

  • Negotiate and close to a signed SOW, with the Chief Commercial Officer joining larger deals.

  • Run the full sales cycle: discovery, solution scoping, proposal, negotiation, close.

  • Translate Anthropic's product roadmap and partnership incentives into the client propositions.

  • Keep Anthropic and AWS partner reps informed on the leads they share, and take part in joint pipeline reviews.

  • Keep the CRM current and forecast your deals accurately.

  • Bring buyer objections and patterns from each industry back to leadership and marketing.

  • Travel for client meetings, up to 30% of your time.

What You Need to Succeed:

  • 2–4 years in a client-facing commercial role in a consulting or IT services firm where you closed deals yourself, such as account executive, account manager, or consultant who owned client sales. Be ready to share the specifics: what you closed, at what size, and how long each deal took.
  • OR experience with banks, insurers, or pharma/biotech companies in one of these roles: selling services or technology to them (including smaller deals you closed yourself or larger deals where you supported the lead); working on client projects at a consulting firm, including proposals or scoping; or working inside one of these companies on projects where you helped evaluate and select outside vendors.
  • Working knowledge of Financial Services (banking, insurance, capital markets) or Life Sciences (pharma, biotech). You have worked in the industry or sold into it, and you can discuss a buyer's process and regulatory constraints in their terms.
  • Experience selling services engagements or complex B2B deals with several stakeholders.
  • Clear written and spoken communication with director-, VP- and C-level buyers.
  • Comfort handling a steady volume of leads and choosing where to spend your time.

    • Strong plus

  • Experience selling AI/ML, data or cloud services.

  • Experience working partner-referred leads from Anthropic, AWS, GCP or Azure.

About Provectus:

  • Provectus is an Artificial Intelligence consultancy and solutions provider, helping businesses achieve their objectives through AI and data-driven innovation organization-wide in such industries as Financial Services, Insurance, Healthcare & Life Sciences, Retail & CPG, Media & Entertainment, and Manufacturing.
  • We are recognized by industry analysts as a leading provider of AI solutions across key business domains.
  • At Provectus, we value innovation, ownership, and collaboration — and we are looking for people who want to grow with us and make an impact.

Why Join Us:

  • Leads arrive every day, so your time goes into closing rather than prospecting.
  • You learn enterprise AI consulting sales in two regulated industries.
  • You close with support: our architects scope the work with you, and the Chief Commercial Officer joins larger negotiations.
  • The delivery team can execute what you sell: 350+ people, 150+ certified architects, and 100+ customers in production.
  • Work at the intersection of two AI partnerships: Anthropic and AWS.
  • High-impact role with direct visibility to leadership.

    • Compensation and benefits

  • Base $90–120K + commission, OTE range $140–170K. The salary range is determined through interviews and a review of the education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities of the applicant, and alignment with market data.
  • B2B contract model or full-time model.
  • Unlimited vacation policy.
  • Generous health, vision, and dental insurance, and life insurance.
  • 401(k) matching plan.

Molina Healthcare of Kentucky is hiring a Program Manager, Health Plan Payment Integrity (Claims & Recovery). This position is remote.

Highly Qualified Candidates Will Have the Following -

  • Managed care experience
  • Strong Medicaid experience, Medicare, Marketplace (Specifically Kentucky Medicaid preferred, not required)
  • Claims processing and reimbursement knowledge, Claims processing knowledge on the recovery side
  • Good working knowledge of CPT, HCPCS, ICD, and revenue codes

Essential Job Duties

Provides subject matter expertise for oversight, production, and resolution of health plan payment integrity (PI) recovery concepts. Executes and monitors health plan scoreable action items (SAIs) to ensure performance and quality levels exist in PI Business products and processes. Establishes procedures and techniques to achieve operational goals and executes tasks and projects to ensure Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) and state regulatory requirements are met for pre-pay edits and overpayment recovery. Manages inventory and works in collaboration with PI team to ensure SAI targets are met. Makes independent and informed decisions that contribute to health plan strategy, and acts as a trusted voice in resolving complex business challenges that impact cost-containment and regulatory compliance.

Business Leadership & Operational Ownership
• Independently owns and manages scorable action items (SAIs), including assisting and executing projects and tasks to ensure Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) and state regulatory requirements are met for pre-pay edits, post-payment datamining, and overpayment recovery, to improve encounter submissions, reduce general and administrative (G&A) expenses, and drive positive operational and financial outcomes for all payment integrity (PI) solutions.
• Independently leads efforts to improve claim payment accuracy, claim referrals, adjustment analysis and financial performance.
• Collaborates with operational teams, enterprise stakeholders, and finance partners to proactively identify issues and implement resolution strategies.
• Serves as a thought partner to health plan leadership, and provides well-reasoned recommendations that support short- and long-term business goals.
• Partners with the network team to communicate recovery projects to ensure provider relations is informed and able to respond to provider inquiries.

Strategic Business Analysis

• Uses a business lens to ensure accurate interpretation of provider claims trends, payment integrity issues, and process gaps.
• Applies understanding of health care regulations, managed care claims workflows, and provider reimbursement models to shape payment integrity related recommendations and action plans.
• Translates strategic needs into clear requirements, workflows, and solutions that drive measurable improvement.
• Partners with finance and compliance to develop business cases, and support reporting that ties operational outcomes to financial targets.

Applied Analytical Support

• Uses data analysis tools/systems to support business analysis.
• Validates findings and test assumptions through data, and leads with contextual knowledge of claims processing, provider contracts, and operational realities.
• Creates succinct data summaries and visualizations that enable faster leadership decision-making.

Required Qualifications

• At least 5 years of business analyst experience in a managed care organization (MCO), and at least 3 years of experience in Medicaid and/or Medicare programs, or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.

Preferred Qualifications

raw.description:
Head of Marketing
Build the marketing engine behind the next stage of Tiro's growth.
About Tiro
Tiro is growing with purpose.
We partner with employers across science, technology and advanced manufacturing to solve one of the biggest challenges facing UK industry: building the workforce capability needed to innovate, grow and compete.
For over 15 years we've helped employers develop specialist talent through apprenticeships, but we're building something much bigger. We're becoming a trusted workforce capability partner, helping organisations think differently about skills, productivity and long-term workforce development.
To achieve that ambition, we need a marketing function that's every bit as ambitious as the business itself.
Why this role?
This isn't a role for someone who wants to manage campaigns. It's for someone who wants to shape markets. The industries we support are concerned with productivity, succession planning, skills shortages, retention and growth. Your job is to help them connect those problems with solutions they may never have considered.
You'll build a marketing function that starts with customer problems, not products. You'll develop compelling propositions, create vertical-specific campaigns, strengthen our brand, generate demand and build a marketing engine that contributes directly to commercial growth.

The Opportunity

You'll have the freedom to shape how marketing operates, how success is measured and how marketing works alongside Employer Growth, Employer Success, Product and Delivery.

You'll influence executive thinking, help shape commercial strategy and play a key role in helping Tiro achieve its ambitious growth plans.

If you enjoy building functions, creating clarity from complexity and using customer insight to drive commercial decisions, you'll find plenty to get excited about here.
What you'll be doing

You'll:
  • Build and lead a commercially focused marketing function that generates demand, pipeline and brand awareness.
  • Develop customer-led propositions, messaging and positioning that connect with employers across our priority sectors.
  • Create full-funnel marketing strategies that move audiences from awareness through to meaningful commercial conversations.
  • Build segmentation, Ideal Customer Profiles and campaign strategies that improve targeting and conversion.
  • Partner closely with Employer Growth to ensure marketing contributes directly to pipeline quality and commercial performance.
  • Use customer insight, market research and campaign performance data to continually improve strategy and decision-making.
  • Develop our brand profile through content, thought leadership, PR, events and storytelling that builds trust and credibility.
  • Coach and develop the marketing team, creating clear priorities, accountability and a culture of continuous improvement.

This role is for you if...

You've:
  • Led B2B marketing teams with direct accountability for pipeline, customer acquisition or revenue growth.
  • Built, transformed or professionalised a marketing function, team or operating model.
  • Influenced founders, executives or Boards and been prepared to challenge an established view with evidence.
  • Operated successfully where resources, structure and information are imperfect.
  • Used customer insight and Customer voice to materially change a proposition, positioning or commercial strategy.
  • Marketed complex, technical or consultative propositions where value needs explaining rather than being immediately obvious.
  • Developed ICPs, segmentation, vertical strategies, propositions and messaging around genuine customer problems.
  • Created demand in markets where customers were not necessarily already looking for the solution.
  • Built strong Marketing–Sales alignment, including CRM discipline, lead qualification, sales enablement and shared commercial priorities.
  • Used data and experimentation to understand what is and isn't working, stopping or changing activity rather than defending it.
  • Built credibility through thought leadership, content, PR, events, partnerships and external networks, not simply paid acquisition.
You'll be:
  • Commercially curious & customer obsessed – you get underneath customer problems and the whole growth system, using customer, market and sales insight to understand where the opportunity is and what will drive growth.
  • Builder mentality – you'reenergised by creating what doesn't yet exist, able to build propositions, capability, processes and Marketing–Sales ways of working, while remaining hands-on enough to make them happen.
  • A Momentum Creator – combining pace with judgement, tests rather than assumes, makes decisions without perfect information, adapts quickly when something isn't working and keeps the business moving forward.

Why join Tiro?

This is an opportunity to shape far more than a marketing plan.
You'll help define how our business is positioned in the market, influence commercial strategy, build a high-performing marketing function and play a central role in our next phase of growth.

You'll join a business with ambitious plans, a collaborative leadership team and the freedom to make meaningful change.

If you're motivated by creating impact rather than simply delivering activity, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Opportunity

Latino Legendsis recruiting an exceptionalAdministrative Managerto join a rapidly expanding US-based construction firm operating across major metropolitan markets in Texas and Arizona (including Houston, Dallas/Fort Worth, and Phoenix).

Our client specializes in residential turns, rehabs, and service work for institutional real estate partners, alongside commercial and private build projects. They are looking for an experienced operational leader from Latin America who can manage remote administrative talent and run daily workflows with precision.

Position Summary

The Administrative Manager leads the company’s end-to-end administrative operations while supervising a dedicated remote team (Construction Administrative Assistants and a Job Dispatcher).

This is a true working-manager position. Beyond mentoring and leading your team, you will personally manage core administrative workflows—including job setup, change orders, billing, documentation, client communications, compliance records, and leadership reporting. The ideal candidate has managed administrative or operational functions within construction, property management, or the trades, and operates with high autonomy.

Key Responsibilities

Team Leadership & Allocation

  • Supervise, mentor, and evaluate the Construction Administrative Assistant team and the Job Dispatcher.

  • Distribute and balance workloads across regional markets and Project Managers, adjusting coverage as project volumes fluctuate.

  • Set clear performance standards, lead regular check-ins, conduct performance coaching, and partner with the VP of Operations on talent strategy.

  • Lead recruiting, interviewing, and onboarding for new additions to the remote administration team.

Core Operations & Job Administration

  • Build and maintain job files in JobTread, tracking scopes, budgets, timelines, and client data.

  • Process change orders, purchase orders, lien waivers, and billing submissions via client portals.

  • Handle direct communications with clients, property managers, and homeowners via phone and email regarding job progress, scheduling, and documentation.

  • Step in to support direct reports during capacity surges or planned absences.

Company Administration & Compliance

  • Oversee full-cycle onboarding and offboarding for staff and contractors (system provisioning, Gusto setup, documentation, equipment tracking).

  • Maintain complete personnel records, contractor agreements, worker classifications, and policy sign-offs.

  • Manage corporate compliance files, including contractor licenses, certificates of insurance (COIs), vendor agreements, W-9s, and renewal schedules across states.

  • Support accounts receivable and accounts payable workflows, verifying billing accuracy, following up on collections, and tracking weekly AR logs.

  • Deliver regular analytical reports to senior leadership covering job margins, pending change orders, cash receivables, and team output.

Process Standardization & Tooling

  • Write and maintain Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for administrative routines; audit output for quality control.

  • Administer software ecosystems: Google Workspace Admin, JobTread, CompanyCam, and Gusto.

  • Continuously detect operational bottlenecks and roll out scalable workflow enhancements.

Qualifications & Requirements

  • Experience:3+ years in an administrative management or operational supervisor capacity, preferably overseeing remote teams within construction, trades, or property management.

  • Bilingual Fluency:

    • English:Native or near-native proficiency (written and spoken). You will interact daily with US executives, institutional property managers, and homeowners.(A phone screening and written evaluation are required during the selection process).

    • Spanish:Full fluency to effectively coordinate with field crews and trade teams.

  • Industry Acumen:Working knowledge of US construction documentation, including work orders, subcontracts, change orders, purchase orders, lien waivers, client portal billing, and job dispatching.

  • Client & Phone Presence:Strong verbal communication skills, comfortable handling inbound/outbound client calls, status briefings, and conflict resolution.

  • Technical Proficiency:Advanced Google Workspace (Admin Console, Sheets, Docs, Calendar), familiarity with construction platforms (JobTread or equivalent like Procore/Buildertrend), CompanyCam, Microsoft Office, and Gusto.

  • Work Setup:Fully equipped home office located in Latin America with high-speed internet, a dedicated quiet workspace for confidential calls, a reliable backup connectivity solution, and a dependable computer.

Preferred Assets:

  • Prior experience as the lead operations/administrative manager for a US contractor.

  • Direct background managing contractor agreements, insurance compliance, and worker classifications.

  • Hands-on experience with institutional investor portals and construction lien processes.

raw.title: Fullstack React Native Developer
raw.excerpt: The RoleTuneCore Engineering builds the web and mobile applications that power the world’s leading music distribution platform for independent artists.
raw.description:
The Role

TuneCore Engineering builds the web and mobile applications that power the world’s leading music distribution platform for independent artists. We’re looking for a Fullstack React Native Developer to help build our next-generation mobile experience — someone equally comfortable shipping polished React Native features and building the Rails APIs that power them.

This is a senior-level role: you’ll own significant technical scope, set direction on mobile architecture and practices, and mentor other engineers, while staying hands-on in the codebase.

What You’ll Do

  • Design, build, and maintain cross-platform mobile applications using React Native for iOS and Android from a single codebase

  • Build and maintain the Rails API endpoints that power the mobile app — request/response contracts, background jobs, and data models the client depends on

  • Work closely with product, design, and backend engineers to translate designs and wireframes into high-quality, reusable code across the full stack

  • Integrate RESTful APIs and third-party SDKs; optimize app performance, responsiveness, and stability

  • Write unit and integration tests, and help shape our mobile testing strategy as we build out React Native end-to-end coverage

  • Debug and resolve platform-specific issues, including native modules and bridging

  • Manage app store submissions and release processes for both the App Store and Google Play

  • Stay current with the React Native ecosystem and mobile best practices, and bring relevant updates back to the team

  • Uphold TuneCore’s core mission, vision, and values in the code you ship and the decisions you make

Leadership Expectations

  • Provide technical leadership on mobile architecture decisions, balancing durability and scalability against delivery speed

  • Set and evolve coding standards and best practices for the mobile codebase

  • Give effective, constructive code review feedback to other engineers

  • Mentor and guide engineers on the team in both technical growth and career development

  • Research and recommend new tools and technologies where they’d meaningfully improve the team’s output

  • Skills and Attributes

  • 6+ years of experience writing production code, including 3+ years building and shipping mobile applications

  • Strong proficiency in React / React Native, and in JavaScript/TypeScript

  • Demonstrated fluency with Ruby on Rails in production — building and maintaining API-only Rails services, not just “a web framework of some kind”

  • Familiarity with state management approaches (we currently use React Query and Context API)

  • Experience with Git, CI/CD pipelines, and mobile release workflows

  • Understanding of mobile UI/UX principles and platform guidelines (Apple HIG, Material Design)

  • Experience with REST APIs and async data handling; GraphQL a plus

  • Experience with native iOS (Swift/Objective-C) or Android (Kotlin/Java) a plus, but not required

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience

Salary Transparency

TuneCore is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The base salary range for this position is $120,000-$135,000. The final salary offer will be determined by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s relevant experience, specialized skills, internal equity, and specific work location. This range represents our good faith estimate at the time of posting.

Where you'll be

This role will be remote. TuneCore operates on a hybrid model giving our teams flexibility and choice in how they work. Employees have the option to work from our office 8 days per month on a flexible schedule organized at the department level.

Other Duties

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive list of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Our Values:

TuneCore is a team of creators, for creators. Our mission is to support our artists and labels at every stage of their careers. Our driving forces are fairness, expertise, respect and transparency. As global citizens, we believe that if we build more diverse, equitable and inclusive teams across our company, we will collectively create and offer more innovative solutions and better serve our artists, labels, partners, and employees.

We strive to build a company that reflects the communities we serve and embraces the diversity of the world we live in, where each person’s unique perspective is valued, and where everyone has the same opportunities and is supported in their personal and professional growth. From our hiring practices to the culture we create and nurture, we are committed to listening, learning and evolving. Our goal is to make TuneCore an inspirational place that feels comfortable and familiar no matter how you look, where you call home, who you love, what you believe, or what’s on your playlist.

CSR Strategy: Shaping Music for Good

Our core values are put into action through Shaping Music for Good, Believe and TuneCore’s global corporate social responsibility strategy, integrated at all levels of the company and at the heart of our business model.

We strive to shape the music industry for good by building trusting relationships with artists and partners, investing in the growth and talent development of our local markets, and empowering our community to positively impact society. We work to achieve progress on our core priorities: gender equity, diversity, equity & inclusion, environmental sustainability, and wellness for our employees, artists, and industry partners.

Shapers Program

Employees have the opportunity to join the Shapers Program, a resource group made up of teammates who want to dedicate their time and skills to Shaping Music For Good initiatives. Shapers develop action plans, educate teammates, support the implementation of programs, and inspire action within the organization on causes and issues that align with TuneCore and Believe’s SMFG priorities.

Inclusion in the Music Business Report

In 2025, Believe and TuneCore partnered with the Annenberg Inclusion Initiative, the world’s leading think tank studying diversity and inclusion in the entertainment industry, to produce the second Inclusion in the Music Business report which analyzes the gender, race, and ethnicity among executive leadership in the music industry.

Recognition and Awards:

  • Fast Company's 10 Most Innovative Companies in Music list (2023-2025)

  • Crain's Best Places to Work in NYC (2022-2024)

Benefits & Perks:

At TuneCore we’re committed to the well-being of our employees and aim to create a workplace that fosters both personal and professional growth. Our inclusive benefits include, but are not limited to:

  • Paid Time Off including vacation, holidays, paid bereavement, unlimited paid sick days, and company-wide week off between Christmas and New Years—every employee needs time to take care of themselves and their family.

  • “Wellness Fridays” year-round (close at 1pm on Fridays)

  • Universal Paid Parental Leave for both parents - because we know your newest family member(s) deserve your undivided attention.

  • Comprehensive health, vision, dental, FSA and dependent care from day 1 of employment - your health comes first.

  • 401k match - an investment in your future.

  • Company wide events, outings and volunteer days – we have team spirit and know how to have fun!

  • Hybrid Work - employees have the option to work primarily remotely and work from the office 8 days per month on a flexible schedule organized at the department level, in accordance with Company policies.

  • Learning and development opportunities and career development training – we believe in promoting and growing our leadership from within the company and proactively invest in our people.

  • Free distribution subscription for employees – so you can experience the magic of releasing music worldwide (and give us valuable feedback!).

TuneCore and Believe are Equal Opportunity Employers. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive work environment. We encourage applicants of all backgrounds to apply. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Before TuneCore, artists needed to be signed to a record label to sell their music online. In 2006, we democratized the industry by partnering directly with digital stores and streaming platforms to enable any musician to sell their songs worldwide while retaining 100% ownership of their music. Today, TuneCore is the leading independent development partner for self-releasing artists to build audiences and careers, with technology and services across distribution, publishing administration and a range of promotional services. TuneCore is headquartered in Brooklyn, NY, and owned by Paris-based Believe, one of the world’s leading digital music companies. The company is one of the fastest growing companies in the music industry and is actively investing in the continued growth of the business.

We have made it our mission to best serve artists and labels at each stage of their development in the digital world. We are a company that cares deeply about our people and our creator community, advocating for diversity, equity, and inclusion across all of our platforms and throughout our business. The pursuit of innovation inspires us to work hard for our artists, while collaboration drives the way we work and approach our company’s social responsibility.
